_note: Declaration for scripts/check_explainer_text.py. The application is not a place to leave notes for the operator. Every fact this checker knows is in this file, not in the script; the floor lives in explainer_baseline.json so check_ratchets_not_loosened.py can see it move.

surfaces.why: the kit's own default copy reaches every screen that does not override it

explainer-paragraph.why: A muted paragraph of static prose is where a mechanism gets explained. Interpolated text is excluded on purpose: a paragraph carrying a value is reporting STATE ('Showing the first 100 of 340'), and state is not an explainer.

format-teaching-placeholder.why: A placeholder naming a FORMAT teaches the format. 'Write the note in Markdown.' is the reported case. A placeholder naming the CONTENT ('One-line summary') is not this and stays.

help-that-explains.why: A Field's help is the other place explainers hide, usually restating the label and then teaching what the value does downstream. A short help that names units or an example is not this.

exempt._why: An empty state names an ACTION and stays; that is design rule 9, which requires an instructional hint. These props are how the kit passes one.
